controls.description: Capital expenditure, including the capitalisation of repairs and major maintenance, requires documented approval against the entity's capitalisation criteria before the amount is recognised as an asset.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Approved capital expenditure request forms with a completed capitalisation-criteria checklist and authorising signature.
controls.limitations: The approver may not fully understand the accounting criteria; the control can be bypassed by miscoding expenditure or by collusion.
controls.objective: Ensure only expenditure meeting the capitalisation criteria is recognised as property, plant and equipment.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Finance reviews the repairs and maintenance expense accounts each period for items that appear capital in nature, and reviews capital additions for items that appear to be repairs, investigating and correcting anomalies.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Periodic review working papers with follow-up notes and correcting entries where applicable.
controls.limitations: A review detects only what the reviewer notices; subtle misclassifications near the capitalisation boundary may pass unchallenged.
controls.objective: Detect misclassification between repairs expense and capital additions.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Management reviews depreciation rates, methods, useful lives and residual values at least annually, approves any changes, and documents the rationale for the conclusions reached.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Signed annual review memorandum with supporting analysis of asset usage, condition and technological change.
controls.limitations: The review is only as good as the information and challenge applied; management may retain favourable lives to flatter profit.
controls.objective: Ensure depreciation reflects the expected pattern of consumption of future economic benefits.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: The fixed asset system calculates depreciation automatically from approved asset master data; any change to a depreciation rate, method or useful life requires independent authorisation and is logged.
controls.evidence_of_operation: System change logs and authorisation records for master-data amendments.
controls.limitations: Does not address whether the approved lives are appropriate; an authorised but inappropriate life will still be applied consistently.
controls.objective: Prevent unauthorised or undocumented changes to depreciation parameters.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: All disposals of property, plant and equipment require prior written authorisation and completion of a disposal form, which is forwarded to finance so the asset is removed from the register and the ledger.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Authorised disposal forms filed with derecognition entries; sequential control over disposal forms.
controls.limitations: Ineffective if operations staff dispose of assets without completing the form, or if forms are not forwarded to finance.
controls.objective: Ensure every disposal is authorised and removed from the accounting records.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Physical verification of fixed assets is performed periodically by persons independent of custody; differences between the physical assets located and the register are investigated and the register corrected.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Verification sheets, investigation notes and approved register adjustments.
controls.limitations: Detects missing assets only at the verification date; cannot identify exactly when an asset was disposed of.
controls.objective: Detect assets that no longer exist but remain on the register.
controls.responsible_role: Internal audit / finance, independent of custody
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Management performs an assessment of impairment indicators for each asset or cash-generating unit at each reporting date and documents the conclusion, including the basis for concluding that no formal impairment test is required.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Impairment indicator checklist or memorandum, signed off and dated.
controls.limitations: Management may overlook or downplay indicators, particularly where an impairment charge would be unwelcome; the assessment needs genuine challenge.
controls.objective: Ensure impairment indicators are identified so that impairment testing is performed when required.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Operating and financial performance of significant assets or cash-generating units is monitored against budgets and forecasts, and adverse variances are investigated for possible impairment indicators.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Management accounts with variance commentary; investigation notes for adverse variances.
controls.limitations: Performance information may be prepared on a basis that obscures asset-level underperformance; investigation quality varies.
controls.objective: Provide timely warning of underperformance that may indicate impairment.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Major maintenance and replacement work orders identify the component replaced and are routed to finance so the carrying amount of the replaced part can be derecognised when the new part is capitalised.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Work orders cross-referenced to derecognition entries in the fixed asset register.
controls.limitations: Relies on maintenance staff correctly identifying replaced components and on the information reaching finance.
controls.objective: Ensure replaced significant parts are removed from the carrying amount.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

controls.description: Significant assets are componentised in the fixed asset register, with major parts recorded separately and depreciated over their own useful lives.
controls.evidence_of_operation: Fixed asset register showing component-level records for significant assets.
controls.limitations: Componentisation at initial recognition requires judgment about which parts are significant; retrospective componentisation of old assets may be impracticable.
controls.objective: Enable separate depreciation and derecognition of significant parts.
controls.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Capital expenditure request forms that cite no criteria or show approval after the asset was recognised.
evidence.description: The entity's written policy stating the criteria for capitalising expenditure as property, plant and equipment, including the treatment of repairs, replacements and major maintenance.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Approved, dated, and consistent with the applicable financial reporting framework.
evidence.limitations: A policy proves intent, not compliance; consistent application must still be tested.
evidence.name: Capitalisation policy
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability as audit evidence of actual accounting treatment is limited: it describes what should happen, not what did. It is corroborative only when combined with tests of application.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Invoices describing work that is clearly capital in nature within the expense accounts, or vice versa.
evidence.description: The repairs and maintenance expense ledger with supporting supplier invoices, work descriptions and amounts for the period.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Complete population for the period; invoices identify the nature of the work performed.
evidence.limitations: Internally processed; descriptions on invoices may be vague or misleading.
evidence.name: Repairs and maintenance ledger and supporting invoices
evidence.reliability_notes: Source documents from third-party suppliers are more reliable than internal descriptions alone; reliability falls where descriptions are vague, as judgment is then required about the nature of the work.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Additions recognised without any approval form, or approvals signed by the requestor.
evidence.description: Capital expenditure approval forms showing the nature of the expenditure, the capitalisation criteria considered, and independent authorisation.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Completed before recognition, signed by someone independent of the requestor, referencing the criteria.
evidence.limitations: Approval evidences authorisation, not the correctness of the accounting judgment.
evidence.name: Capital expenditure approval records
evidence.reliability_notes: More reliable where the approver is independent and the form requires explicit consideration of the criteria; a signed form alone does not prove the judgment was correct.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Physical assets that cannot be matched to register entries, or register entries with no supporting acquisition record.
evidence.description: The detailed fixed asset register showing cost, accumulated depreciation, depreciation rate/method, useful life and net book value by asset or component.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Reconciled to the general ledger; changes in the period identifiable.
evidence.limitations: Internally maintained; reflects the entity's own judgments about lives and methods.
evidence.name: Fixed asset register
evidence.reliability_notes: The register is the item under test, not corroboration of it; reliability for audit purposes comes from the auditor's independent recalculation and inspection, not from the register itself.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Recalculation differences that management cannot explain.
evidence.description: The auditor's independent recalculation of the depreciation charge for sampled assets, based on cost, rate, method and useful life.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Prepared independently by the auditor, showing inputs, formula and agreement to the recorded charge.
evidence.limitations: Proves arithmetic accuracy only; does not address whether the lives and methods themselves are appropriate.
evidence.name: Auditor's depreciation recalculation
evidence.reliability_notes: High reliability for accuracy of the calculation: generated directly by the auditor from source inputs. Reliability of the conclusion still depends on the appropriateness of the underlying lives and methods.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Review memoranda that merely assert lives are unchanged with no supporting analysis.
evidence.description: Management's documented annual review of depreciation rates, methods, useful lives and residual values, with supporting analysis.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Dated, signed, addressing usage, condition, technological change and residual values.
evidence.limitations: Management-prepared; may lack genuine challenge, particularly where longer lives flatter profit.
evidence.name: Management's useful-life review documentation
evidence.reliability_notes: Inquiry and inspection of this document alone is weak evidence; reliability increases only where the auditor corroborates the conclusions with independent evidence (usage data, condition, industry practice).
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Disposal forms completed after the asset has already left the premises, or proceeds banked with no disposal form.
evidence.description: Disposal authorisation forms recording the asset disposed of, the method and date of disposal, and authorising signatures.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Completed before or at disposal; authorised independently of the person handling the asset.
evidence.limitations: Only evidences disposals that were documented; undocumented disposals leave no form.
evidence.name: Asset disposal authorisation forms
evidence.reliability_notes: More reliable where authorisation is independent and forms are sequentially controlled; cannot provide evidence about disposals that bypassed the process.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Proceeds with no matching derecognition entry, indicating the asset may still be on the register.
evidence.description: Records of proceeds from sale or scrap of assets: sales invoices, weighbridge tickets, bank receipts.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Identifiable to the specific asset disposed of; dated in the correct period.
evidence.limitations: External proceeds evidence (bank receipt) is stronger than internal sales records; proceeds alone do not prove the correct gain or loss was calculated.
evidence.name: Disposal proceeds records
evidence.reliability_notes: Bank receipts and third-party buyer documentation are relatively reliable evidence that a disposal occurred; the accounting for the disposal still requires separate testing.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Verification sheets signed off without any differences ever being reported, suggesting the exercise was perfunctory.
evidence.description: The auditor's record of assets selected from the register and physically located (or not), with identifying details and condition notes.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Recorded independently at the time of inspection, identifying asset, location and whether it was found.
evidence.limitations: Covers only the assets inspected; absence of a selected asset requires follow-up, not automatic conclusion.
evidence.name: Auditor's physical verification notes
evidence.reliability_notes: High reliability for existence of the assets inspected: obtained directly by the auditor through observation. A missing asset is an exception to investigate, not proof of a particular cause.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Adverse indicators (idle assets, losses) with no documented consideration.
evidence.description: Management's documented assessment of impairment indicators at the reporting date, including the conclusion and its basis.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Addresses internal and external indicator categories; signed off and dated.
evidence.limitations: Management-prepared and judgmental; may omit inconvenient indicators.
evidence.name: Impairment indicator assessment
evidence.reliability_notes: Weak as standalone evidence because it reflects management's own judgment; reliability depends on the auditor's independent corroboration of the indicators considered and those omitted.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Forecasts that are consistently optimistic compared with actual outcomes.
evidence.description: Management's budgets, forecasts and business plans for the assets or cash-generating units under review.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Approved, internally consistent, and reconcilable to information used elsewhere.
evidence.limitations: Forward-looking and inherently uncertain; susceptible to management bias.
evidence.name: Management forecasts and budgets
evidence.reliability_notes: Reliability depends on the track record of forecasting accuracy and the degree of independent challenge; the auditor treats forecasts as assumptions to be tested, not as facts.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Market data that contradicts management's recoverable amount conclusions.
evidence.description: External data relevant to recoverable amount: market prices for similar assets, industry reports, valuer reports.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Independent of the entity; relevant to the specific asset and measurement date.
evidence.limitations: May not be directly comparable; external valuers' work must itself be evaluated.
evidence.name: External market or valuation data
evidence.reliability_notes: Generally more reliable than internal estimates because it is independent of management; reliability still depends on relevance, comparability and the competence of the source.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Replacement work with no corresponding derecognition entry in the register.
evidence.description: Maintenance and replacement work orders describing the work performed, the component replaced, dates and costs.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Identify the specific component replaced; cross-referenced to the asset record.
evidence.limitations: Internally prepared; may not identify the replaced component with enough precision to quantify derecognition.
evidence.name: Major maintenance and replacement work orders
evidence.reliability_notes: More reliable where work orders are prepared by operational staff at the time of the work and independently of the accounting decision; reliability for the accounting conclusion still requires linkage to the register.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

evidence.contradictory_evidence: Significant assets recorded as single lines with no component breakdown.
evidence.description: Component-level detail in the fixed asset register for significant assets, showing separately identified major parts and their useful lives.
evidence.expected_characteristics: Major parts separately identified with their own depreciation parameters.
evidence.limitations: Reflects the entity's own judgments about significance and lives.
evidence.name: Component register detail
evidence.reliability_notes: The register detail is the item under test; its reliability for the audit conclusion comes from the auditor's testing of the underlying judgments, not from the record itself.
evidence.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: The entity's capitalisation policy and how it is applied in practice; the volume and nature of repairs and maintenance expenditure; whether performance measures reward reported profit.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where repairs and maintenance expenditure is material and capitalisation involves judgment. Less applicable where the entity expenses all repairs by policy, or where expenditure is immaterial.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: the repairs-versus-capital boundary is a recognised area of judgment and a common source of misstatement; the factor describes the absence of the disciplined assessment that would contain it.
factor_risk.explanation: Where capitalisation decisions are made without a documented assessment against clear criteria, expenditure that merely maintains an asset can be recognised as an asset. This is a risk factor - an indicator of where misstatement could occur - not evidence that any particular amount is misstated.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Material repairs and maintenance expenditure exists and capitalisation decisions are made without documented assessment against capitalisation criteria.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: The depreciation policy, rates and useful lives currently applied; when they were last reviewed and by whom; asset usage, condition and technological environment.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where property, plant and equipment is material and depreciation is significant to profit or the carrying amount. Less applicable to assets measured at revalued amounts with frequent valuations, or where lives are contractually fixed.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: unreviewed depreciation parameters are a recognised cause of misstated carrying amounts; the factor removes the control that would keep them current.
factor_risk.explanation: Depreciation parameters set in the past may no longer reflect how assets are used or how long they will last. Without periodic review, the charge and the carrying amount drift from economic reality. The factor indicates heightened risk; it does not prove the current rates are wrong.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Property, plant and equipment is material and depreciation rates, methods or useful lives have not been reviewed for continued appropriateness.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: How disposals are communicated from operations to finance; whether a disposal process exists; the age and nature of assets on the register.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where the entity regularly disposes of, scraps or replaces assets. Less applicable where disposals are rare, individually significant and closely managed (though the register should still be tested).
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: the completeness of derecognition on disposal is a standard audit concern; undocumented disposals are a recognised cause of overstated asset registers.
factor_risk.explanation: If operations can dispose of assets without telling finance, the register retains assets that no longer exist. The missing communication is a control deficiency; the resulting overstatement is a potential misstatement that must be tested for, not assumed.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Assets are disposed of, scrapped or demolished and there is no reliable process ensuring finance is informed so the register can be updated.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether any assets or operations show signs of underperformance, idleness, damage or adverse market change; how management currently considers impairment.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies wherever indicators of impairment may exist. Irrelevant only where no indicators exist - which itself requires the assessment the factor says is missing; the auditor must therefore form an independent view.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: unrecognised impairment where indicators exist is a recurring source of material misstatement; the absence of any indicator-assessment process is a recognised gap.
factor_risk.explanation: Impairment is only recognised if indicators are first noticed. Without a process to look for them, indicators such as idle assets or loss-making operations can persist unaddressed and carrying amounts remain overstated. The factor is a gap in detection, not proof of impairment.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: No process exists to identify and evaluate indicators of impairment at the reporting date.

factor_risk.additional_info_needed: Whether significant assets are componentised; how replacement expenditure is described in work orders; the scale of replacement programmes in the period.
factor_risk.applicability: Applies where significant parts of assets are replaced (overhauls, refurbishments, major component swaps). Less applicable where assets have no separately significant components or replacements are immaterial.
factor_risk.confidence_basis: Established audit practice: failure to derecognise replaced parts is a recognised error in component accounting; the factor describes the missing information flow that causes it.
factor_risk.explanation: Capitalising the new part is only half the entry: the replaced part's carrying amount must be removed. If maintenance information never reaches finance, or the old part was never separately identified, the old cost stays in the carrying amount alongside the new cost. This is a potential misstatement to test for, not an established error.
factor_risk.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factor_risk.trigger_condition: Significant components are replaced in the period and there is no process ensuring the replaced part is derecognised.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where the entity incurs material repairs and maintenance expenditure and the accounting treatment involves judgment - for example major overhauls, refurbishments, or replaced parts. Less relevant where the entity's policy is to expense all repairs.
factors.description: Expenditure on repairs and maintenance is added to the cost of property, plant and equipment (or recognised as a separate asset or component) without a documented assessment of whether it meets the entity's capitalisation criteria - for example, whether it enhances future economic benefits beyond the asset's originally assessed standard of performance, or merely restores that performance.
factors.name: Repairs and maintenance expenditure capitalised without adequate assessment
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Repairs and maintenance expense unusually low relative to the asset base or industry norms; large round-sum additions described as refurbishment or upgrades; additions capitalised near the year-end; inconsistent treatment of similar expenditure between periods.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where property, plant and equipment is material and depreciation significantly affects profit or carrying amounts. Less relevant for assets measured at revalued amounts with frequent valuations, or where useful lives are contractually fixed.
factors.description: Depreciation is charged using rates, methods or useful lives that have not been reviewed for continued appropriateness, or that do not reflect the actual pattern of consumption of the assets' future economic benefits - for example, rates carried forward unchanged for many years despite changes in usage, technology or asset condition.
factors.name: Depreciation rates, methods or useful lives not reviewed or inappropriate
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Fully depreciated assets still in active use; depreciation charge inconsistent with the age profile of the asset base; useful lives markedly different from industry practice without explanation; no documented review of lives and residual values.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where the entity regularly disposes of, scraps, demolishes or replaces assets. Less relevant where disposals are rare and individually significant, though the register should still be tested.
factors.description: Assets that have been sold, scrapped, demolished or otherwise disposed of remain on the fixed asset register and in the general ledger, because disposals are not communicated to finance or are processed without proper documentation.
factors.name: Disposed assets not removed from the accounting records
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Assets on the register that cannot be located; disposal proceeds banked with no matching derecognition entry; insurance schedules or tax filings listing fewer assets than the register; very old fully depreciated assets still carried.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant wherever indicators of impairment could exist - loss-making operations, idle assets, physical damage, or adverse market or technological change. The absence of an assessment process is itself the gap.
factors.description: Management has no process to identify and evaluate indicators that an asset (or cash-generating unit) may be impaired - such as significant underperformance, physical damage, adverse market or technological changes, or assets that are idle or held for disposal.
factors.name: Impairment indicators not identified or evaluated
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Loss-making operations or product lines; idle or mothballed assets; observable declines in market values; adverse regulatory or technological developments; carrying amounts above recent transaction prices for similar assets.

factors.conditions_relevant: Relevant where significant parts of assets are replaced - overhauls, refurbishments, major component swaps. Less relevant where assets have no separately significant components or replacements are immaterial.
factors.description: When a significant part of an asset (for example an engine, a roof, or a major liner) is replaced, the carrying amount of the replaced part is not removed from the asset's cost, so both the old and the new component remain reflected in the carrying amount.
factors.name: Replaced significant components not derecognised
factors.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
factors.warning_signs: Major replacement or overhaul programmes with no corresponding derecognition entries; components not tracked separately in the register; additions capitalised where the replaced part's original cost was never separately identified.

procedure_evidence.notes: Policy sets the criteria the tested items are judged against.
Ledger and invoices are the population vouched.
Approval records evidence the control operation tested.
Policy is inspected for clarity and consistent application.
Expense trends are the subject of the analytical procedure.
Register provides the inputs (cost, rate, life) for recalculation.
Recalculation workpaper is the output and primary evidence.
Management's review is inspected and challenged.
Lives and methods in the register are evaluated for reasonableness.
Change logs in the register evidence authorisation of amendments.
Verification notes are the primary output of this procedure.
Register is the population selected from.
Disposal forms are inspected for authorisation and completeness.
Proceeds records corroborate that disposals occurred.
Absence of forms for known disposals is itself a finding.
Proceeds without derecognition indicate unrecorded disposals.
Management's assessment is inspected for completeness.
Forecasts are inspected for signs of underperformance.
External data corroborates or contradicts management's view.
The assessment identifies which assets require testing.
Forecast assumptions are the inputs challenged.
External data provides independent challenge to assumptions.
Work orders are the population inspected for derecognition.
Component detail shows whether the old part was separately identified.
Componentisation is directly inspected.
Work orders corroborate which components were replaced.

procedures.exception_criteria: Expenditure capitalised that does not meet the capitalisation criteria; repairs of a capital nature left in expense; inconsistent treatment of similar items.
procedures.expected_result: Each tested item is correctly classified: capitalised items meet the recognition criteria and are supported and approved; repairs are expensed.
procedures.follow_up: Quantify the misclassified amounts and propose adjustments; if misclassification is pervasive, extend testing across the additions and repairs populations and reconsider the risk assessment. Do not assume intent - errors and bias require different responses.
procedures.objective: Determine whether expenditure near the repairs-versus-capital boundary has been correctly classified.
procedures.population: Repairs and maintenance expense and capital additions for the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Targeted selection: large or round-sum items, refurbishments, year-end additions, and items with vague descriptions; supplement with a random sample if the population is large.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain the repairs and maintenance expense ledger and the capital additions listing for the period.
Select items near the capitalisation boundary: large refurbishments, overhauls, year-end additions and vaguely described items.
For each selected item, inspect the supplier invoice and work description to establish the nature of the work performed.
Evaluate whether the expenditure meets the entity's capitalisation criteria (enhancement of future economic benefits beyond the originally assessed standard of performance) or is a repair.
Verify that capitalised items were approved and that the accounting treatment is consistent with similar items.
procedures.title: Test the classification of repairs and maintenance expenditure

procedures.exception_criteria: No written policy; policy unclear on the repairs boundary; evidence that the policy is not followed in practice.
procedures.expected_result: A clear, approved policy exists that addresses the repairs-versus-capital boundary, and tested transactions are consistent with it.
procedures.follow_up: Where the policy is absent or unclear, treat the classification risk as higher and extend substantive testing; discuss the gap with management as a control deficiency.
procedures.objective: Establish the criteria the entity claims to apply and test whether approval controls operated.
procedures.population: Capitalisation policy and capital expenditure approvals in the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Inspect the policy in full; test a sample of approval forms across the period.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Inspect the entity's capitalisation policy for clarity on repairs, replacements and major maintenance.
Select a sample of capital expenditure approval forms and verify they were completed before recognition and authorised independently of the requestor.
Check that the forms evidence consideration of the capitalisation criteria, not just budget approval.
Note instances where expenditure was recognised without approval as control exceptions.
procedures.title: Inspect the capitalisation policy and test approval controls

procedures.exception_criteria: Repairs expense significantly below expectation without a convincing operational explanation; a shift of expenditure from repairs into additions.
procedures.expected_result: Repairs and maintenance expense is consistent with expectations given the asset base, activity levels and prior periods; significant variances are explained and corroborated.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate unexplained variances by selecting the underlying items for vouching; a persistent, unexplained decline in repairs expense alongside rising additions indicates higher classification risk.
procedures.objective: Identify unusual patterns in repairs expenditure that may indicate misclassification.
procedures.population: Repairs and maintenance expense by month and by asset class, with capital additions for comparison.
procedures.sampling_notes: Not a sampling procedure; set an investigation threshold based on materiality.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Develop an expectation for repairs and maintenance expense based on prior periods, the size and age of the asset base, and activity levels.
Compare actual expense to the expectation and investigate significant variances.
Compare the trend in repairs expense with the trend in capital additions for offsetting movements.
Corroborate explanations with operational evidence, not inquiry alone.
procedures.title: Perform analytical procedures over repairs and maintenance expense

procedures.exception_criteria: Recalculated charge differs materially from the recorded charge; incorrect rates, lives or methods applied to sampled assets.
procedures.expected_result: The recalculated depreciation charge agrees with the recorded charge for each sampled asset, using the approved rate, method and useful life.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate the cause of each difference (data error, wrong parameter, formula fault); quantify the effect across the population; if parameters were wrong, refer to the evaluation of useful lives.
procedures.objective: Verify the arithmetical accuracy of the depreciation charge.
procedures.population: Depreciation charge for the period by asset.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample across asset classes and acquisition years; include assets added and disposed of in the period (part-year calculations).
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain the fixed asset register with cost, depreciation rate, method and useful life by asset.
Independently recalculate the depreciation charge for each sampled asset, including part-year calculations for additions and disposals.
Compare the recalculation with the recorded charge and investigate differences.
Agree the approved parameters used to the depreciation policy and any authorised changes.
procedures.title: Recalculate depreciation for a sample of assets

procedures.exception_criteria: Useful lives or methods that are not supportable given asset usage, condition, technological change or industry practice; lives extended without justification.
procedures.expected_result: Useful lives, methods and residual values are reasonable and consistent with how the assets are used, their condition, and observable technological or market change.
procedures.follow_up: Where lives are not supportable, estimate the effect of reasonable lives on the charge and carrying amount; discuss with management and consider a control deficiency where the review process failed.
procedures.objective: Assess whether the depreciation parameters themselves are appropriate, not just accurately applied.
procedures.population: Depreciation policies, lives and methods by asset class.
procedures.sampling_notes: Focus on material asset classes and on classes showing warning signs (e.g. fully depreciated assets still in use).
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Inspect management's documented review of useful lives, methods and residual values.
Challenge the conclusions: compare lives with actual asset usage and condition, technological change, and industry practice.
Investigate warning signs such as fully depreciated assets still in active use or lives extended without documented justification.
Evaluate whether changes in estimates have been accounted for prospectively and disclosed where required.
procedures.title: Evaluate the appropriateness of useful lives and depreciation methods

procedures.exception_criteria: Changes to rates, methods or lives made without independent authorisation or without documentation; unauthorised access to asset master data.
procedures.expected_result: All changes to depreciation parameters in the period were independently authorised, documented and logged.
procedures.follow_up: Treat unauthorised changes as control exceptions; establish who made them and why; extend testing to the affected assets' charges.
procedures.objective: Test whether changes to depreciation parameters are controlled.
procedures.population: All changes to depreciation rates, methods or useful lives in the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of changes if few; sample if numerous, weighted toward changes reducing the charge.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Extract the log of changes to depreciation parameters in the asset master data for the period.
For each selected change, inspect the authorisation and the documented rationale.
Verify the authoriser was independent of the person requesting or entering the change.
Confirm the change was applied from the correct date.
procedures.title: Test authorisation of changes to depreciation parameters

procedures.exception_criteria: Selected assets that cannot be located; assets found in a substantially different condition or location from the records.
procedures.expected_result: Each sampled asset exists, is identifiable, and is in the recorded location and apparent condition.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate each missing asset: confirm whether it was disposed of, scrapped, transferred or stolen; if disposed of, verify the accounting treatment; a pattern of missing assets indicates the register is unreliable and testing must be extended.
procedures.objective: Obtain direct evidence that recorded assets still exist.
procedures.population: Fixed asset register at the reporting date.
procedures.sampling_notes: Sample across locations and asset classes, weighted toward portable, high-value and older assets; include some fully depreciated assets.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Select a sample of assets from the fixed asset register.
Locate each sampled asset physically and confirm its identity (asset tag, serial number or description).
Note the asset's location and apparent condition, and any discrepancies with the register.
For assets that cannot be located, record the details for follow-up investigation.
procedures.title: Physically verify a sample of assets from the register

procedures.exception_criteria: Disposals without authorisation; proceeds that do not agree to supporting records; gains or losses incorrectly calculated; derecognition in the wrong period.
procedures.expected_result: Each tested disposal was authorised, completely removed from the register and ledger in the correct period, and the gain or loss correctly calculated.
procedures.follow_up: Quantify misstatements in gains, losses and carrying amounts; investigate unauthorised disposals with management; consider whether missing authorisations indicate a wider control failure.
procedures.objective: Verify that recorded disposals are genuine, authorised and correctly accounted for.
procedures.population: All disposals recorded in the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of material disposals; sample smaller ones.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain the listing of disposals recorded in the period.
For each selected disposal, inspect the disposal authorisation form and confirm it predates or coincides with the disposal.
Trace proceeds to supporting records (sales invoices, weighbridge tickets, bank receipts).
Recalculate the gain or loss on disposal and verify the asset was removed from the register and ledger in the correct period.
procedures.title: Inspect disposal records and verify the accounting for disposals

procedures.exception_criteria: Evidence of disposals (board minutes, insurance changes, proceeds) with no corresponding derecognition; assets known to have been scrapped still on the register.
procedures.expected_result: No material unrecorded disposals are identified; where identified, they are quantified and adjusted.
procedures.follow_up: Quantify the carrying amount of unrecorded disposals and propose adjustments; report the communication breakdown between operations and finance as a control deficiency.
procedures.objective: Detect disposals that occurred but were never recorded.
procedures.population: Board minutes, insurance schedules, proceeds records and operational reports for the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Targeted search rather than statistical sampling; focus on asset-intensive operations and sites with turnover of equipment.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Review board minutes and operational reports for mention of asset sales, scrapping, demolitions or site closures.
Compare insurance schedules and, where available, tax asset listings with the fixed asset register for assets that have disappeared.
Inspect bank receipts and sales records for disposal proceeds with no matching derecognition.
Follow up each indication with operations and finance staff and inspect the register treatment.
procedures.title: Search for unrecorded disposals

procedures.exception_criteria: Indicators exist that management's assessment did not consider; assessment is undocumented or perfunctory.
procedures.expected_result: Management's assessment addresses the relevant internal and external indicator categories and its conclusion is consistent with the auditor's own observations.
procedures.follow_up: Where indicators were missed, perform the auditor's own indicator assessment and, where indicators exist, require or perform impairment testing; treat a perfunctory assessment as a control deficiency.
procedures.objective: Evaluate whether management's impairment indicator assessment is complete and reasonable.
procedures.population: Management's impairment indicator assessment at the reporting date.
procedures.sampling_notes: Not a sampling procedure; covers the assessment as a whole, focused on material assets and cash-generating units.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Inspect management's documented assessment of impairment indicators, covering internal sources (obsolescence, damage, underperformance, idleness) and external sources (market declines, technological, regulatory or economic change).
Inquire of operational and finance management about asset performance, idle capacity and market developments.
Compare the assessment against the auditor's own knowledge from other audit work (site visits, analytical procedures, board minutes).
Document indicators identified by the auditor that management omitted.
procedures.title: Evaluate management's impairment indicator assessment

procedures.exception_criteria: Significant adverse trends or variances that indicate possible impairment and have not been addressed by management.
procedures.expected_result: Analytical procedures either identify no indicators of impairment, or the indicators identified are consistent with those management has addressed.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate each unaddressed indicator; where it suggests an asset may be impaired, proceed to testing of the recoverable amount.
procedures.objective: Use analytical procedures to independently identify possible impairment indicators.
procedures.population: Asset-level or cash-generating-unit performance data, market data and industry information.
procedures.sampling_notes: Not a sampling procedure; set investigation thresholds with regard to materiality.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Analyse trends in revenue, margins and utilisation for significant assets or cash-generating units against budgets and prior periods.
Compare carrying amounts with observable market data for similar assets where available.
Consider external information: industry downturns, technological change, regulatory developments.
Investigate adverse variances and trends with management, corroborating explanations.
procedures.title: Perform analytical procedures to identify impairment indicators

procedures.exception_criteria: Recoverable amount below carrying amount with no impairment recognised; key assumptions that are not supportable or inconsistent with other audit evidence.
procedures.expected_result: Where indicators exist, an impairment test has been performed using supportable assumptions, and any required impairment loss (and related disclosures) is recognised.
procedures.follow_up: Challenge unsupported assumptions and quantify the effect of reasonable alternatives; propose adjustments for unrecognised impairment; evaluate the implications for the audit opinion if management refuses.
procedures.objective: Test the impairment measurement where indicators of impairment exist.
procedures.population: Assets or cash-generating units where impairment indicators have been identified.
procedures.sampling_notes: Census of material assets/CGUs with indicators; judgmental selection below materiality.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Where indicators exist, obtain management's impairment test (value in use or fair value less costs of disposal).
Evaluate the reasonableness of key assumptions: cash flow forecasts, growth rates, discount rates - and their consistency with other audit evidence.
Test the mathematical accuracy of the model and the completeness of the cash-generating unit's carrying amount.
Verify that any impairment loss is recognised in the correct period and that required disclosures are made.
procedures.title: Inspect impairment tests and challenge key assumptions

procedures.exception_criteria: Replacement expenditure capitalised with no derecognition of the replaced part; replaced part's carrying amount unknown because it was never separately identified.
procedures.expected_result: For each tested replacement, the replaced component has been derecognised (or its carrying amount estimated and removed where it was not separately identified), and only the new cost remains capitalised.
procedures.follow_up: Quantify the double-counted carrying amount and propose adjustments; where components were never separately identified, evaluate whether estimation of the replaced part's carrying amount is required; report the information-flow gap as a control deficiency.
procedures.objective: Verify that replaced significant components have been derecognised.
procedures.population: Major maintenance, overhaul and replacement work orders capitalised in the period.
procedures.sampling_notes: Targeted selection of the largest replacement programmes and overhauls; census where few.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Obtain the listing of capitalised replacement and major maintenance expenditure for the period.
For each selected item, inspect the work order to identify the component replaced and the nature of the work.
Trace the item to the fixed asset register and verify that the replaced component's carrying amount was derecognised at the same time the new cost was recognised.
Where the replaced part was not separately identified, evaluate the reasonableness of management's estimate of its carrying amount.
procedures.title: Inspect replacement work orders and verify derecognition of replaced parts

procedures.exception_criteria: Significant assets recorded as single lines with no component breakdown; major parts with materially different useful lives depreciated as one.
procedures.expected_result: Significant assets are componentised with major parts separately identified and depreciated over their own useful lives.
procedures.follow_up: Where componentisation is absent, assess whether the resulting depreciation and derecognition errors could be material; discuss the gap with management.
procedures.objective: Test whether significant assets are appropriately componentised.
procedures.population: Significant assets recognised or revalued in the period, and major asset classes.
procedures.sampling_notes: Focus on high-value, complex assets (plant, buildings, aircraft, networks).
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Identify significant assets with major parts that have different useful lives or consumption patterns.
Inspect the register to confirm those parts are recorded as separate components with their own depreciation parameters.
Evaluate the reasonableness of the significance judgments and the allocated costs.
Consider the implications for depreciation accuracy and for future derecognition.
procedures.title: Test componentisation of significant assets

procedures.exception_criteria: Work performed does not match the work order description; replaced components still recorded as in use.
procedures.expected_result: The physical work observed is consistent with the work orders tested, supporting the accounting for replacements and derecognitions.
procedures.follow_up: Investigate inconsistencies between observed work and recorded work orders; extend inspection where descriptions appear unreliable.
procedures.objective: Corroborate the nature of replacement work through direct observation.
procedures.population: Major replacement or overhaul work in progress or recently completed.
procedures.sampling_notes: Judgmental selection of accessible, significant replacement work.
procedures.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
steps: Identify significant replacement or overhaul work in progress or recently completed.
Observe the work and the components involved, noting what is being replaced.
Compare observations with the work order descriptions and the register treatment.
Document the corroboration obtained for the derecognition conclusions.
procedures.title: Observe significant replacement work

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where repairs and maintenance expenditure is material and the capitalisation decision involves judgment.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Whether expenditure is a repair (expense) or an improvement (asset) is a classification decision in the transaction stream; incorrectly capitalised repairs misclassify revenue expenditure as capital expenditure.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where questioned capitalised amounts are material to the property, plant and equipment balance.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Capitalised costs increase the asset's carrying amount and reduce the current period expense; inappropriate capitalisation therefore overstates the carrying amount of property, plant and equipment.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant wherever property, plant and equipment is material; the carrying amount is the direct product of the depreciation parameters.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Depreciation rates, methods and useful lives determine accumulated depreciation and hence the carrying amount; inappropriate parameters misstate the carrying amount of property, plant and equipment.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where the depreciation charge is material to profit or loss.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: The depreciation expense recognised in the period must be accurately calculated in accordance with the entity's policy; wrong rates or lives produce an inaccurate charge.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where disposals, scrapping or demolitions have occurred or are suspected.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: Assets that have been disposed of no longer exist at the reporting date; if they remain recognised, the existence assertion for the recorded balance is misstated.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where the net book value of unrecorded disposals could be material, and no offsetting proceeds or losses have been recorded.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: The carrying amount continues to include the net book value of assets that are gone, overstating property, plant and equipment.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where impairment indicators exist; the assertion is not assumed to be misstated merely because the assessment process is absent.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: If indicators of impairment exist and no impairment loss is recognised, the carrying amount may exceed the recoverable amount.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where impairment losses are recognised or where indicators were identified but no loss recognised; disclosure of the judgments made may be required.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: The judgments and assumptions underlying impairment conclusions, and the events giving rise to recognised losses, may require disclosure; an absent assessment process also means required disclosures may be missed.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where significant components have been replaced in the period.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: The replaced component no longer exists as part of the asset; if its carrying amount remains recognised, the existence assertion for that portion of the balance is misstated.

risk_assertions.conditions: Relevant where the carrying amount of replaced components could be material.
risk_assertions.why_relevant: The carrying amount includes both the old component's remaining cost and the new component's cost - the same economic capacity counted twice - overstating property, plant and equipment.

risk_controls.explanation: Directly addresses the factor by requiring the capitalisation criteria to be considered and evidenced before recognition.
Detects misclassifications that the approval control missed, on both sides of the repairs/capital boundary.
The periodic review is the control that should keep depreciation parameters current; its absence is the factor.
Prevents unauthorised changes to parameters, though it does not address whether authorised parameters are appropriate.
Directly addresses the factor by creating the communication channel from operations to finance that is currently missing.
Detects assets that have disappeared without being recorded as disposals.
The indicator assessment is the missing process described by the factor.
Performance monitoring provides the information on which an indicator assessment depends.
Creates the information flow from maintenance to finance that the factor says is missing.
Componentisation makes derecognition of the replaced part practicable by separately identifying its carrying amount.

risk_procedures.reason: Directly tests the classification decision at the heart of the risk.
Establishes the criteria and tests whether the approval control operated.
Analytical procedures highlight unusual patterns suggesting systematic misclassification.
Verifies the charge is accurately calculated from the approved parameters.
Addresses the core of the risk: whether the parameters themselves are appropriate.
Tests whether changes to parameters are controlled.
Direct evidence of existence for recorded assets.
Tests that recorded disposals are genuine and correctly accounted for.
Searches for the unrecorded disposals the factor makes possible.
Evaluates the assessment process whose absence is the factor.
Provides the auditor's independent identification of indicators.
Directly tests whether replaced parts were derecognised.
Tests the componentisation that makes derecognition practicable.
Corroborates the nature of replacement work through observation.

risks.causes: Judgment involved in distinguishing repairs from improvements; pressure to report higher profits by deferring expense recognition; absence of a documented capitalisation policy or inconsistent application; approval processes that address budget but not accounting treatment.
risks.description: Revenue expenditure on repairs and maintenance may be capitalised as property, plant and equipment even though it does not meet the recognition criteria for an asset. The result is overstated assets and understated expenses for the period, with overstated depreciation in future periods.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with the volume of expenditure near the capitalisation boundary, the complexity of the asset base, and where performance measures reward reported profit. The presence of this factor does not prove that a misstatement exists; it identifies where the auditor should direct attention and professional skepticism.
risks.potential_consequences: Property, plant and equipment may be overstated. Profit for the period may be overstated because expenses are understated. Future depreciation charges will be overstated.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Inappropriate capitalisation of repairs and maintenance expenditure

risks.causes: Depreciation parameters set at initial recognition and never revisited; changes in asset usage, technology or condition not reflected; deliberate extension of useful lives to reduce the charge; errors in the asset register.
risks.description: Depreciation may be understated or overstated, and the carrying amount of property, plant and equipment misstated, because the rates, methods or useful lives applied do not reflect the expected pattern of consumption of the assets' future economic benefits.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with the age and technological sensitivity of the asset base and where small changes in lives have a material effect on profit. The presence of this factor does not prove that a misstatement exists; the current parameters may still happen to be reasonable, which is what the auditor must evaluate.
risks.potential_consequences: The depreciation charge for the period may be materially misstated. The carrying amount of property, plant and equipment may not reflect the consumption of economic benefits. Changes in estimates may be applied incorrectly (retrospectively instead of prospectively).
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Incorrect depreciation charges and carrying amounts

risks.causes: No communication channel between operations (which disposes of assets) and finance (which maintains the register); disposals processed informally or by staff unaware of the accounting implications; scrapping and demolitions treated as non-events.
risks.description: Assets that have been sold, scrapped, demolished or otherwise disposed of may continue to be recognised in the fixed asset register and the general ledger. The existence assertion for the recorded balance is then misstated, and gains or losses on disposal may be wrong.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with the volume of disposals, the number of sites, and the physical portability of assets. The presence of this factor does not prove that a misstatement exists; it is a control deficiency that creates the opportunity for overstatement, which the auditor must test for.
risks.potential_consequences: Property, plant and equipment may be overstated by the net book value of assets that no longer exist. Gains or losses on disposal may be misstated or omitted. Depreciation may continue to be charged on assets that are gone.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Disposed assets remain recognised in the accounting records

risks.causes: No assigned responsibility for impairment reviews; management optimism or reluctance to recognise losses; indicators emerging gradually and going unnoticed; complex cash-generating unit structures that obscure underperformance.
risks.description: Where indicators of impairment exist but are not identified or evaluated, impairment losses may not be recognised and the carrying amount of assets may exceed their recoverable amount.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases where assets are exposed to technological change, market downturns or restructuring, and where cash-generating units are defined broadly enough to mask underperforming assets. The presence of this factor does not prove that a misstatement exists; no impairment may in fact be required, but that conclusion must be evidenced, not assumed.
risks.potential_consequences: Carrying amounts may exceed recoverable amounts, overstating assets and profit. Required disclosures about impairment judgments and recognised losses may be omitted.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Unrecognised impairment losses

risks.causes: Maintenance information never reaching finance; replaced parts never separately identified in the register; work orders that describe the new work but not what was removed; focus on capitalising the new cost while overlooking derecognition.
risks.description: When a significant component of an asset is replaced, the carrying amount of the replaced part may remain in the asset's cost alongside the cost of the new part. The same economic capacity is then counted twice in the carrying amount.
risks.inherent_risk_notes: Risk increases with the scale of replacement and overhaul programmes and where assets were never componentised. The presence of this factor does not prove that a misstatement exists; some replacements may be correctly treated, which the auditor verifies rather than assumes.
risks.potential_consequences: Property, plant and equipment may be overstated by the carrying amount of replaced components. Depreciation in future periods will be overstated. The existence assertion is affected for the replaced portion of the balance.
risks.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md
risks.title: Replaced significant components not derecognised

rules.name: Repairs capitalised without assessment -> classification and valuation risk
rules.rationale: Capitalisation without documented assessment against clear criteria is a recognised source of misclassification between expense and asset. The rule directs the auditor to test the classification boundary substantively (vouching near-boundary items), to inspect the policy and approval controls, and to use analytical procedures to spot systematic shifts - with per-assertion reasoning explaining why classification and valuation are affected.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: The entity's capitalisation policy and how it is applied in practice.
The volume and nature of repairs and maintenance expenditure in the period.
Whether performance measures create pressure to report higher profits.
then.note: The factor is a risk indicator, not evidence of misstatement: each tested item must be judged against the criteria, and inconsistent treatment investigated rather than assumed to be intentional.

rules.name: Unreviewed depreciation parameters -> charge and carrying amount risk
rules.rationale: Depreciation parameters set in the past drift from economic reality without periodic review. The rule directs the auditor beyond arithmetical accuracy (recalculation) to the appropriateness of the parameters themselves (evaluation against usage, condition and industry practice), plus testing of change controls.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: The depreciation policy, rates and useful lives currently applied.
When the parameters were last reviewed, by whom, and with what conclusion.
Information on asset usage, condition and technological change.
then.note: Accurate application of inappropriate parameters still produces a misstatement: recalculation alone is insufficient without evaluating the parameters.

rules.name: Disposals not communicated -> existence risk for recorded assets
rules.rationale: When operations can dispose of assets without finance being informed, the register retains assets that no longer exist. The rule directs the auditor to direct existence testing (physical verification from the register), to test recorded disposals, and to actively search for unrecorded disposals.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: How disposals are currently communicated from operations to finance.
The volume and nature of disposals, scrapping and demolitions in the period.
The age profile and locations of assets on the register.
then.note: The factor is a control deficiency (missing communication), not proof of overstatement: each missing asset found must be investigated to establish what happened to it.

rules.name: No impairment indicator process -> unrecognised impairment risk
rules.rationale: Impairment is only recognised if indicators are first noticed; without a process to look for them, carrying amounts can remain overstated. The rule directs the auditor to evaluate management's assessment (or its absence), to independently identify indicators through analytical procedures, and to test measurement where indicators exist.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: Whether any assets, operations or markets show signs of underperformance, idleness, damage or adverse change.
How management currently considers impairment, if at all.
The definition and composition of cash-generating units.
then.note: The absence of an assessment process does not prove impairment exists; the auditor must form an independent view on indicators before concluding on measurement.

rules.name: Replaced components not derecognised -> double-counted carrying amount
rules.rationale: Capitalising a replacement without derecognising the replaced part counts the same economic capacity twice. The rule directs the auditor to trace replacement work orders to derecognition entries, to test componentisation, and to corroborate the work through observation.
rules.source_reference: Professional practice guidance; standards references unverified - see docs/REFERENCES.md

missing_information: The scale of replacement and overhaul programmes in the period.
Whether significant assets are componentised in the register.
How replacement work is described in work orders and communicated to finance.
then.note: Derecognition is the other half of the replacement entry: testing only the capitalised cost would miss the double-count.
